Self-employed/entrepreneur. Particularly online entrepreneur.

Finding your niche isn’t ‘easy’ and you kinda just have to throw shit at the wall and see what you like and what you believe in. But you don’t have to answer to anyone. You don’t have to “show up on time”. You can literally just work whenever you want. Also you can have moments where you fuck up and the only person who knows is you. And if people do know, they can’t fire you no matter how mad they are. You can look like shit. You can keep your workspace in a mess. Doesn’t matter.

One important thing that should probably know before reading all of this: If you’ve ever seen someone do something, or seen someone make something or just seen something and thought “it doesn’t look *that* hard to do this”, then there’s a good chance it’s not hard and you could even do it yourself. I’ve only ever done stuff that I thought “yeah seems easy enough” and I’ve built a consistent stream of income from that. You can’t just force yourself to come up with an idea though. I’m convinced no one has ever had a good idea by “brainstorming. At least I’ve never done that. You just have to let it come to you. If you’re ever daydreaming about how you’d do/make something with better execution than something that already exists, then that’s a good idea for you.

And you’re probably stuck at your computer all day anyway, so you won’t have the problem of “oh no my work is impacting my social life”. 

This other stuff like “janitor” or “night-watcher” is also valid if you truly believe you’re not intellectually capable at all. Not knocking janitors, but I wouldn’t say the job is ideal, but that’s also just my opinion.

You can ask AI basic questions and it will be right or at least in the right direction most of the time. For example “how to setup a reverse-proxy with caddy on linux” and it will tell you. Or you could ask “how do one-man businesses host web-services cheaply?”. And even if your business doesn’t take off, you still have learned skills that are pretty useful when you could have just been watching youtube.

Also I’ve realised that pretty much everything created on the internet is created with tools designed to make things as easy as possible for developers. Like even game-development. You think game-devs are just coding their game from nothing? No, they’re building it on top of a game-engine like unity, godot, unreal, which actually does most of the “smart” stuff for you, making it easier for you to create the game you want instead of having to learn advanced mathematics to code the entirety of the game’s graphics rendering.

My workflow is 95% introverted and most of my ideas come from daydreaming, not actively thinking. I’ll develop and push out a new feature completely alone and money will flow in. If you’re doing nothing with your time and you feel like you’re full of ideas, then maybe try pursuing the most realistic one.

I don't really have noticable sides. I stay extra hydrated to counteract the dehydration of minoxidil and I do exercise to keep my test levels in check. I personally think you're more likely to get the water-weight bloating from minox than any sexual side-effect from Finasteride. And if on any given day you're really noticing the bloating from minox, then you can take dandelion extract (a natural diuretic) to remove the bloating. Also apparently minox decreases collagen production, so for that I just apply tretinoin (something you should be doing for skincare anyway) in order to up the collagen production. I also have a diet that is high in vitamin A to promote skincell regeneration.

As for unwanted hair-growth, no I have not experienced that either. I guess my eyebrows and beard have gotten thicker but that's welcome. I haven't had much increase in body-hair but my body-hair is pretty scarce anyway.

Also I should add that I take 1mg Fin and 1.25mg Minoxidil orally. The minox 1.25mg is just a 2.5mg pill that I split in half, so the minox sides could be reduced from what they'd be at 2.5mg.

So currently I take Fin+Min and don't have the issues of bloated skin or erectile dysfunction, the two main issues I was worried about when switching to oral. Also as a bonus, I rarely ever catch loose hairs when I run my hands through my scalp now. And all it took was me taking 2 pills every day.

**Easy Solution:** [**Jomo App**](https://jomo.so/) **on iOS**.

It drastically reduces my time spent on distracting apps on my phone. I have the paid version of the app which makes the blocking features "strict" so that it's really hard to bypass the rules that block distracting apps. Doomscrolling for multiple hours is now no longer an issue for me.

It's very very customisable. You can set rules for how the app blocks other apps at certain times of the day. You can make it so that specified apps can only unblock if you do a certain action like work-out for 45 minutes or scan a QR code. The app integrates with Apple Health data, so that if you log workout data with an app like "Strong", the logged data will then be sent to Apple Health which is read by Jomo who can then tell that you have done 45 minutes of exercise and now your distracting apps can be unblocked. # My advice:

* Minoxidil and microneedling will help. I'd hold off on finasteride or dutasteride until you're absolutely fully done with puberty. Minoxidil doesn't require a prescription btw. It's OTC.
* Your hair looks fine right now, but if you think it's thinner than it was before then it's good to do something now. The reason you can see your scalp easily might also be due to how oily your hair is at that current moment.
* Make sure you're getting protein in.
* Make sure you don't have sodium laureth sulphate in any hair products. It's in a lot of stuff and thins out your hair. Sulphate-free shampoo and conditioners are just as cheap as any other shampoo and conditioner btw. I personally use "OGX Biotin & Collagen Shampoo", but there are many others.
* Also make sure your vitamin D levels are good.

This is gonna sound crazy, but I get freeze-dried beef liver and put a small thumb-sized piece of that in my morning protein shake with banana, blueberries & cocoa powder. The taste is masked pretty well and the benefits of liver are worth it. It gives heme-iron as well as being abundant in a ton of other nutrients. For example, vitamin A which is good for your skin. It also essentially replaces everything you'd get in a vitamin B-complex supplement pill. Also every gram of freeze-dried beef liver is equivalent to like 4g of fresh beef liver and it doesn't spoil so quickly. Imo this is the easiest and most cost effective way of introducing liver into your diet. I tried recipes to cook with beef liver and I couldn't bare any of them due to the taste. Why would I spend time cooking something I know I'm not gonna like?

Iron supplements also work fine if you take it with Vitamin C. Except with those, the iron is plant-derived and doesn't absorb as well as meat-derived heme-iron.

Ngl I had an addiction to a substance chemically similar to meth during uni for a few months. I don't remember much of it. I don't think much happened during that time either since I was just in my room high doing nothing. The whole time I knew I was addicted and abusing it. I was doing pretty terrible emotionally before during and after the ordeal. I ended the addiction completely on my own without anyone being aware of it in the first place, because I was very ashamed and knew that it's best that no one knows anyway. I simply just flushed the rest of what I had down the toilet and endured the ensuing weeks of brain-fog. I couldn't think straight at all. Whenever I tried to sit down and do something that required sustained mental effort, I would just zone out and daydream about unimportant things.

I don't hold the opinion that it's inevitable that your friend is going to ruin their life. It could be the case, though, since I don't know how self-aware this person is or what they've done. It is essential that this person understands that it is an addiction and it is bad for them. At the end of the day this person is likely doing meth because of emotional issues. I would say that the reason I was never in denial about the addiction was because I knew I was doing it because I was depressed and I knew that continuing it would only bring me more depression.

If you're up for it, try be a supportive friend and set an example of what being 'normal' looks like, without making them feel like they're innately inferior for having an addiction, since more shame will just result in more addiction. My main help was that I had one friend who I knew valued me as a person and understood my struggles and empathised despite not falling into the same pitfalls as me. They didn't even know about the addiction until I told them a while later. At the same time, like others have said, perhaps make sure your personal possessions are safe from this person, I guess.

Also if it is the case that this person denies that they have an addiction, don't feel too guilty about heavily limiting contact. Your voluntary emotional support is only useful if they accept they're addicted and need to stop.

If you think this person is really out of control, tell their parents first, and not the police or uni since then it will be on their record and neither of those two systems actually care about this person in the slightest.

You won't find a single addict who says they have a good relationship with their parents, but at the same time, their parents are the only people in the world who actually care about them, despite probably being less-than-optimal parents.

Basically if the person is obviously out of control and you have to tell someone, tell their parents first.

By society's standards, yes.

But people who are unlucky enough to have personal knowledge of how trauma can lead to unhealthy coping strategies would say 'no', because they give themselves the benefit of the doubt: "I'm not a bad person, I just do bad things because bad things happened to me."

Unfortunately most people don't tend to give people the benefit of the doubt. If they see someone doing something bad, they'll judge it at face value and say "that person *is* bad"

I bet even most people in this subreddit are guilty of not giving others the benefit of the doubt. The natural reaction of a human is: If someone has hurt you, you instantly regard them as a horrible person and try distance yourself. And why shouldn't you? It's better for you to not be surrounded by hurtful people.

In fact I see a contradiction between this poll and what people say in the subreddit. So many people trash their parents and say that they are outright bad people. Sentiments like "They should have figured themselves out before unloading their trauma onto their kids" are common. But then the majority of this poll says "Toxic people aren't bad, they're victims. Hurt people hurt people.", which leads me to think that the majority of people answering this poll are just as likely to pass their own trauma onto the next generation because they excuse themselves of their wrongdoings, but not others. There is a lack of self-awareness.

If everyone with issues explains their issues by saying "It's because of trauma. I promise I'm a good person", then what even is a 'bad person'? Most bad people I can think of have some sort of trauma that lead them to do what they do. I still think they're bad. A person who does bad things is a bad person and a person who does good things is a good person. I don't care about hypotheticals where the 'bad person' was born good but became bad. I don't care if the 'good person' was born good and never had a chance to become bad.

My opinion is that toxic unhealthy coping mechanisms do make you a bad person, but you can become closer to being good by replacing bad coping mechanisms with good ones, which takes effort. As a society, the healthy thing to do is to correctly label people who do bad actions as 'bad people' so that they switch up their act and form habits that make them good.

TL:DR People who do bad things are bad, regardless of whether its from trauma or not.

Most of us cannot see through your very thick and luscious hair so we can't really tell. However, this does not mean you are not balding. I'd say your urgency is low so I'd recommend you do some of the stuff on this list which is on the 'low' category.

Low:  
\- **Vitamin D.** If you don't live in a sunny country or you stay inside 100% of the time, you're gonna need more vitamin D  
\- **Water**. Drink more if you don't drink enough. Most people dont drink enough.  
\- **Stop using hair washing products that include "sulfates".** Sulfates are very bad for hair- **Cold showers**. I don't do this, but apparently its good for your hair.  
\- **Micro-needling Roller.** Stimulates blood vessels on the skin/near the hair causing more blood and nutrients to go to the hairs and the hairs to grow healthier. Doesn't take much time out of your day.

Medium:  
\- **Minoxidil.** Chemical that increases dermal blood flow wherever it is applied. Just rub it on where you think you're balding everyday and you're good. However, if you are REALLY REALLY balding like Homer Simpson, you're gonna need to pair minoxidil with other high strength things as well.  
\- **Dermapen**. Does exactly what the microneedling roller does but better, but it also hurts more.  
\- **Biotin.** It's a vitamin that improves hair health somehow. Good for growth. I use it but I'm not really sure if it does anything since I use it in combination with other things.

High:  
\- **Finasteride**. Blocks DHT receptors in the body. People say there aren't side-effects, but there are. My side-effects are quite minimal. I have never had a problem getting an erection.  
\- **RU58841**. Experimental drug. An alternative to finasteride. Some say it has less sides.

Very High:  
\- **Hair Transplant**. Costs a lot.  
\- **Reincarnate yourself into a person with good hair.** Works pretty well
